comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Slot 3 of the 2026-09-02 parallel round worked this card. What landed is on `main3`; what did not is `a_2IoXIHzri`. Against the five things this card says today is far from the vision:

**A tab belongs to a machine.** Not done, and the largest thing left. MIP-2 is Accepted and carries the whole design, including the durability answer the Draft was waiting on: degrade per tab, and every tab that exists today is single-machine and keeps the guarantee it has. Carded as `a_2IoXIHzri` with the reason it was not started - stages three and four land together or not at all, because stage three alone replaces "every machine on screen at once" with "one tab fills the window" and stage four is what gives the side-by-side back.

**A machine always gets a column.** Falls out of the same change. `a_2I6h18OU6` is answered rather than left open and moved out of `uncommitted`.

**A window is not a unit.** Done, in two parts. The bug is fixed - a window somebody asked for opens onto tabs of its own and remembers nothing of anybody else's (`a_2IZ5TL6DQ`). And the unit is built: each window keeps its own arrangement and claims it while it runs, so a window that closes leaves something to come back to. `muster window reopen` and a menu item read it.

**Two windows cannot show one pane.** Measured rather than built, and `a_2IZ6Of6JP` now carries the answer: a herdr client that loses its terminal to a `--takeover` sees its stream end, 258 to 259 ms after the taking client is spawned. That makes handoff nearly free and leaves fan-out - two windows showing one pane at once - the expensive one nobody asked for. README and `muster docs overview` stopped claiming the thing that was never true.

**`pane move` cannot name a tab that does not exist.** Done (`a_2IXGSgZi7`). The core says where a pane is going in Muster's words and the adapter picks herdr's tag.

## The leak, which this card says is ours alone

Two of its three ways in are closed. `Region` and the saved arrangement no longer carry a workspace, and `BackendIntent` no longer names one - the herdr adapter asks the daemon which of its workspaces a pane is in, which is where a defence against one backend's behaviour belongs. The tab is the way in that remains, and it is the whole of `a_2IoXIHzri`.

The glossary still defines a tab as daemon truth, and that is still accurate: a Muster tab is one herdr tab until something groups two. It stops being accurate when `a_2IoXIHzri` lands, and MIP-2 says so.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Slot 1 of the 2026-09-03 parallel round worked the last of this card's five gaps that was ours alone. What landed is on `main1`, as MIP-2 stages three and four (`a_2IoXIHzri`). Against the five:

**A tab belongs to a machine.** Done, and it was the largest thing left. A window holds an ordered list of Muster tabs and shows one; `cmd+1` and `cmd+2` switch between a local tab and a devenv tab the way tabs switch everywhere else. A tab holds a region per machine with panes in it, which is one for every tab until somebody groups two - and `muster pane move --tab`, or dragging a row onto a caption, is what groups them. So one tab can hold a laptop pane beside a devenv pane, which is the sentence this card opened with.

**A machine always gets a column.** Gone with it (`a_2I6h18OU6`, now done). Nothing is owed a column, a machine you have finished with stays empty, and a row per machine at the foot of the agent list is the way back in.

**A window is not a unit.** Was already done on `main3`, and unchanged.

**Two windows cannot show one pane.** Unchanged, and the one thing here that is not ours: it is herdr's frame stream, and `a_2IZ6Of6JP` carries the measurement.

**`pane move` cannot name a tab that does not exist.** Was already done, and it grew the third destination this needed: a tab, named rather than pointed at through one of its panes.

## The leak, which this card said is ours alone

Closed. `Region` no longer carries a workspace, a daemon or a tab - it carries the machine and its share, and the tab owns the list it is in. The saved arrangement names Muster's tabs and Muster's panes and nothing of herdr's. The glossary stops calling a tab daemon truth.

## The bill, paid where the card said to pay it

`docs/architecture.md`'s durability table now has two tiers and says which is which. Every tab that is on one machine keeps every row it had; only a tab somebody deliberately grouped depends on a file of Muster's, and only that one is lost if the file is - as a tab per machine, with every pane still running. A daemon restart reassembles a grouped tab from two halves; a machine that is unreachable leaves the tab showing the half it can.

What is left of this card is the second pile - the restriction - which is not ours: one client per terminal, and `a_2IZ6Of6JP` is where it lives.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A window, a tab and a pane are Muster's own units, and none of them takes its shape from herdr. Stated as the experience wanted rather than a design:

> windows/tabs/panes must be concepts that Muster itself has its own definitions of, completely un-dictated by herdr. They are simply organizational units. Muster should be able to have any permutation of these looking at different daemons/machines/whatever, and it will translate into herdr's domain and ultimately herdr shouldn't care or impose restrictions

What that means in use:

- **A tab holds whatever panes you put in it**, laptop and devenv side by side if that is what the work needs.
- **A window holds whatever tabs you put in it**, and two windows are two independent workspaces rather than two views of one.
- **A pane moves between tabs, and between windows**, by drag or by command, without ending what is running in it.
- **A pane stays on its machine.** It is a process, and processes do not move between machines. This is the one limit that is not herdr's to lift, and it should stay stated so nobody builds on the opposite.
- **Muster translates.** Whatever arrangement you ask for, the adapter works out what herdr has to be told. herdr's workspaces and tabs stop being anything a person using Muster has to know about.

## How far today is from that

Every one of these traces back to the same root - Muster's organizational units are herdr's:

- A tab belongs to a machine, so `cmd+1` and `cmd+2` cannot switch between a local tab and a devenv tab. The window is a column per machine. (`docs/mip/0002-muster-tabs.md`, `a_2HtF52Itm`)
- A machine always gets a column whether you want it or not, and emptying one refills it. (`a_2I6h18OU6`)
- A window is not a unit at all: every window shares one `window.toml`, so a second window opens onto the first one's arrangement. (`a_2IZ5TL6DQ`)
- Two windows cannot show one pane, so a pane cannot be handed from one window to another. (`a_2IZ6Of6JP`)
- `pane move` cannot name a tab that does not exist yet, because the CLI inherited the shape of a drag onto an existing row. (`a_2IXGSgZi7`)

## Two piles, and they need different work

Worth separating, because only one is ours alone.

**The leak.** Muster's own records are built out of herdr's nouns - `Region` carries a daemon, a workspace and a tab; `window.toml` writes herdr ids to disk; the glossary defines "tab" as *"daemon truth"*. Nothing here needs herdr's cooperation. This is the refactor, and `docs/mip/0002-muster-tabs.md` is most of the argument for it already.

**The restriction.** One client per terminal. No amount of Muster-side vocabulary fixes this, because it is a real byte stream off a real PTY, and it is in the least reachable part of herdr: the frame stream is not in the JSON-RPC API at all, it is `herdr terminal session control` over stdio with no published schema. Moving a pane between windows is exactly this problem - window B showing it means window A stops - so the handoff question in `a_2IZ6Of6JP` is the same question. Upstream, or a fan-out where one bridge feeds several surfaces.

## The bill

Durability, and it should be paid knowingly. herdr writing the shape down is why *"quitting Muster costs nothing"* is true today - a Muster that never comes back still leaves the tabs and their trees. A tab spanning two machines can only live in Muster's own file. MIP-2's answer is to degrade per tab: a tab whose panes are all on one machine keeps today's guarantee, and only a genuinely cross-machine one depends on us. That looks right, and it is the thing to confirm before building.

## Next step

MIP-2 is Draft and covers the tab alone. It says it is waiting on somebody driving a two-machine window for a day - that happened (2026-09-01), and it turned up the window findings above, which MIP-2 does not touch. Since it is Draft and nothing depends on it, revising it in place to cover the window and the pane as well is cheaper than superseding it, and its Context and Alternatives sections carry over.
title: 🧩 Windows, tabs and panes are Muster's own units, and a pane moves freely between them
